title: What If the Amazon Rainforest Vanished?

scenes.text: What if the Amazon rainforest vanished? Rain would stop falling far from the forest itself.
The Amazon sends moisture into the air as flying rivers, and that water feeds the South American monsoon.
Without it, rainfall across much of the continent would drop, especially in the west and south.
The forest also stores carbon equal to fifteen to twenty years of today's human CO2 emissions.
Below about one thousand millimeters of rain a year, researchers say, a rainforest cannot exist at all.
Parts of the southeastern Amazon already release more carbon than they absorb. The loss has started.

description:
What if the Amazon rainforest vanished?
Its moisture feeds the rains of a whole continent, and it stores carbon equal to 15 to 20 years of human emissions.
What should we run through next?
